claim: rfx WR-10 compute_waveguide_s_matrix(normalize='flux') S-parameter envelope versus analytic Airy reference across 2 mesh refinement points (dx=[25, 40] um) and 2 geometries (eps_r=[2.0, 4.0]) over the 75.0-110.0 GHz W band passes the broad-E5 magnitude tolerance of 0.05.
claim_scope: broad rfx WR-10 rectangular_waveguide_port compute_waveguide_s_matrix(normalize='flux') versus analytic Airy reference envelope spanning the uniform mesh refinement axis (dx from 25 to 40 um), the frequency axis (75.0-110.0 GHz W band, cutoff ratio 1.27-1.86), and the geometry axis (eps_r in [2.0, 4.0] dielectric slabs). Power-flux extraction (extract_waveguide_s_matrix_flux) eliminates the Z_TE impedance-mismatch error of normalize=False and the round-trip dispersion error of normalize=True diagonal formula. Truth source is independent analytic Airy formula (multi-reflection inside dielectric slab with TE10 modal impedance), not a same-class FDTD reference.

meta.formula: S_slab = rho(1-e^{-2j delta}) / (1 - rho^2 e^{-2j delta})

absorber_discipline.decision: Accepted, not corrected. Regenerating at 0.75 lambda_g costs ~30x wallclock (WR-15 dx25: 961 s/case at 9.0M cells) and buys 1.10-1.20x on the gate-bearing envelope error. Contrast the WR-90 NU lane (#574), where the same change bought 14.4x -- there the absorber genuinely dominated and IS being regenerated. The residual here still scales with dx after the absorber is fixed, i.e. it is mesh-convergent discretization, not an absorber floor.
absorber_discipline.note: NOT probed. The two probed lanes moved only 1.10x/1.20x on the envelope, so a large absorber attribution here is unlikely -- but that is an expectation, not a measurement, and must not be cited as one. Probe this lane before attributing its envelope error.
